summary: Show the bones. The browser's honest defaults are the palette, and comfort is not a goal.
source: Looka §9 · UX Planet §23 · Tilda Brutalism & Neobrutalism · brutalistwebsites.com

link.role: THE default browser link blue. Do not restyle it

visited.role: the default visited colour. Keeping it is the point

teal.role: a raw field colour. Takes INK text (7.3:1), never white

orange.role: a raw field colour. Takes ink (7.0:1)

pink.role: a raw field colour. Takes ink (6.3:1)

acid.role: a raw field colour. Takes ink (17.4:1)

radius.note: 0 everywhere. Above 0 is a comfort decision.

spacing.note: a tidy consistent gutter is banned — gutters vary on purpose

type.note: system monospace, or ONE oversized grotesque. No pairing subtlety.

focus.reason: the flash colour, hard against the element with zero offset — an offset would be a comfort decision. #ff0090 on white is 4.0:1, above the 3:1 that 2.4.13 requires.

banned: transitions and easing on interaction states
motion.note: instant. A transition exists only to make a change comfortable.

copyBudget.note: measure runs LONG here on purpose — a comfortable measure is a comfort decision. But 80ch is a WCAG ceiling, not a taste, so it holds.

a11y.note: brutalism is accidentally one of the most accessible packs: native controls, default link colours, pure black on pure white at 21:1, and no depth system to misread. The honesty that makes it ugly also makes it legible.
a11y.linkRule: Keeping #0000ee underlined is not nostalgia — it is the single strongest clickability signifier that exists, and NN/g's flat-design critique is precisely about packs that threw it away.
a11y.gradientRule: Gradients are permitted ONLY as hard-edged texture — repeating stripes and halftone dots, where every stop is an abrupt colour change. A soft fade is still banned, because a fade exists to make an edge comfortable and comfort is the thing this pack refuses. The ban that matters is on BLUR, not on the gradient function.
a11y.colourRule: Raw, saturated, unmixed field colours. The pack bans 'muted or tasteful colour' — which is a requirement to be loud, not a licence to be plain. Every field colour here carries INK text; none of them carries white, and that is not a coincidence: saturated mid-tones almost never do.

banned: blurred shadows — hard-offset with 0 blur is fine
transitions and easing on interaction states
muted or 'tasteful' colour — this pack is required to be loud
soft gradient fades (hard-edged stripe and halftone texture is fine)
stock photography, illustration systems, icon sets

darkMode.note: Inverts to pure black paper with white ink. The link blue must lighten to #6f9bff or it is 2.3:1 on black — the ONE place this pack's honesty has to bend, because the browser default was never designed for a dark ground.

scroll.headline: scroll-marquee (●)
scroll.reason: the fun one. <marquee> is a 1995 HTML element and a scroll-bound ticker is its honest descendant — motion that admits it is motion.
banned: smooth-scroll — emphatically. The browser's honest defaults ARE the thesis, so lerped scroll is the single most anti-brutalist addition possible
stacking-cards, parallax, video-scrub, text-reveal — all polish

sheet.metaLine: system mono · 3px black · radius 0 · raw field colour · halftone texture · no transitions
tokenTable: none, or one you visibly violate

notes.tokens: The honesty test: if a rule exists only to make the page more comfortable, delete it. Rounded corners, easing, hover fades, blurred shadows, tidy gutters — all out. But note what that leaves IN: raw saturated colour fields, enormous type, hard-edged texture and collage. Brutalism is loud on purpose — it is not the absence of design.
notes.nav: Unstyled links in a row, separated by whatever the browser does. The default blue and the default visited purple both stay — and that is not nostalgia, it is the strongest clickability signifier that exists.
notes.hero: Oversized monospace at .85 leading, flush left, hard against the edge. No centring: a centred layout is a comfort decision, and this pack has no comfort decisions.
notes.button: A native <button> next to a 3px black box. No transition on any state — a transition exists to make a change comfortable, and comfort is the thing being refused.
notes.form: A native input with a 3px border. The error is a black block with the flash colour — loud, immediate, and impossible to miss, which is what an error should be anyway.
notes.card: There is no card, only boxes. 3px borders, no radius, no shadow, and gutters that deliberately do not match — an even gutter is a tidiness decision.
notes.table: A default HTML table with borders turned on. This is as close as any pack in the catalogue gets to shipping raw markup.
notes.overlay: A hard black panel with a 3px border. No scrim blur, no radius, no entrance animation. It appears.
notes.empty: A 3px dashed box and a sentence. Brutalism is the one pack where the empty state needs no softening — bluntness is already the register.
notes.dark: Inverts to pure black. The link blue is the one place this pack's honesty has to bend: #0000ee on black is 2.3:1 and unreadable, so it lightens to #6f9bff. The browser default was never designed for a dark ground.
notes.narrow: Nothing changes except the display size. There is no grid to collapse, no shadow to clip and no elevation to lose — brutalism is the most robust pack in the catalogue at any width.
notes.copy: Measure runs to 90ch, longer than any other pack, because a comfortable measure is a comfort decision. But 80ch is a WCAG ceiling rather than a taste, so the audit still holds it.
